$description: Localization/RTL rules that every screen spec and component recipe must respect. This file references CONTENT ROLES, never hardcoded translated copy — actual translated strings live in web/messages/{en,ar}.json (or the future Android/iOS string resource equivalents), not here.

supportedLocales.independenceRule: UI locale and course-CONTENT language are independent axes — a course's Content Language (design-tokens.json-adjacent field on Course Editor Overview) describes what language the lesson video/text is authored in, and is never coupled to the viewer's own UI language selection. Never encode a screen's UI-locale assumption into course-content fields or vice versa.

layoutDirection.mechanism: logical CSS properties (margin-inline-*, padding-inline-*, inset-inline-*, text-align: start/end) on web; LayoutDirection-aware modifiers on Android/iOS — see design-to-code/shared/spacing.json#/logicalApplication.
layoutDirection.switchBehavior: Selecting a new UI language in Settings (a) swaps all UI strings, (b) flips layout direction app-wide, (c) applies instantly with no navigation away and no app restart — see ux/SCREEN_UX_SPECS.md § 17.

neverMirrors.$description: Duplicated from shared/navigation.json#/rtlMirroring/neverMirrors for discoverability from a localization-first reading path — the two files must stay in sync; navigation.json is the canonical copy.

numeralFormat.rule: Prices/totals/counts always render as Western Arabic numerals regardless of locale — locked decision.

contentRoles.$description: Screen specs reference these ROLE names in their `content` sections, never literal copy. The actual string lives in the app's message catalog under a matching key, resolved per active UI locale.

examples.heroTitle: role: marketing headline — actual copy in web/messages/{locale}.json under landing.heroTitle
examples.emptyStateTitle: role: empty-state heading, varies per screen/context
examples.errorFriendlyMessage: role: user-safe error copy — never raw backend error text

certificateException.rule: A Certificate's own rendered content (name, course title) follows the certificate's authored language direction, which may be LTR regardless of the app's current UI direction — surrounding chrome (Share button, back affordance) follows normal app RTL rules.
